rule_level_problems.rule: (none) - 'Ensure the patient with any of the following is seen promptly by nurse or doctor'
rule_level_problems.problem: The whole 'seen promptly' box is unencoded: BP >= 180/110, systolic < 80, pregnant BP >= 140/90, pulse irregular / >= 100 / < 50, temperature >= 38, glucose < 3 (< 4 if diabetic) or >= 11.1, SpO2 < 92% at rest, SpO2 drop < 87% on exertion. The grammar has no tier below Urgent, which explains but does not remove the gap; the builders should have either encoded these as Urgent with a note, or recorded the omission explicitly. As it stands a patient with systolic BP 70 or glucose 2.5 and no red-box finding gets no priority from this page.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for urgent signs at initial assessment of the patient
rule_level_problems.problem: The task's due_to is (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Clinical finding" "finding")), the root of the finding hierarchy, so the 34-item check list is triggered by any recorded finding whatsoever. For an initial-assessment page a universal trigger is arguably the intent, but it is unlike every other page's presenting-complaint anchor and will attach this list to every encounter; it deserves a deliberate decision rather than a default.

rule_level_problems.rule: Initial assessment: measure MUAC and height in the pregnant patient / ... in the patient with hypertension / ... in the patient with diabetes
rule_level_problems.problem: These encode monitoring schedules that are management by design (out of scope) and do so only partly: 'Weight and height to calculate BMI' measures height but not weight (kg is an available unit); 'once a year', 'at booking visit', 'at 26 weeks', '3-6 monthly if trying to lose weight' schedules are not representable; the conditionals 'fingerprick glucose only if risk factor', 'urine dipstick only if fingerprick glucose >= 11.1' and 'fingerprick glucose only if glucose on urine dipstick on >= 2 occasions' are dropped; Hb, rhesus, syphilis, HIV, urine dipstick and visual acuity have no measurement unit. Harmless as far as they go, but they should not be read as covering the lower half of the page. The hypertension task also uses only the active_condition trigger while the diabetes task uses both forms (inconsistent).

summary: The red box is fully and correctly encoded: all 21 criteria map to existing SNOMED concepts with the right qualifiers and and/or structure in both the check_for task and the Urgent priority evaluation, and the conditional glucose check is encoded exactly. The main gap is the 'seen promptly' box: eleven of its twelve thresholds (BP, pulse, temperature, glucose, SpO2) appear nowhere in the file, partly because the grammar has no priority tier below Urgent, leaving systolic BP < 80 or glucose < 3 without any priority from this page. Minor points: the check_for task fires on any clinical finding at all, and the chronic-condition measure tasks cover only fragments of the (out-of-scope) monitoring schedules.
